manifest.prompt: a button with custom bezier curve hover state animations that makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal, but practical for a website
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 32 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=32, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' ethereal-button.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' ethereal-button.metadump.json
3. Also pull the anti-keywords and review prompts (checks) for your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' ethereal-button.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' ethereal-button.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' ethereal-button.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: A button that stays still at rest and lets light carry the hover: a soft halo and a faint lift brought in on a slow, hand-set cubic-bezier, using only transform and opacity, with focus and reduced-motion each offered an equivalent.
essence.summary: Soft halo, slow hand-set bezier settle, compositor-only properties, visible focus, reduced-motion fallback.

formula.full: primary button + soft halo in the primary hue + hand-set cubic-bezier hover on transform and opacity + visible focus-visible ring + reduced-motion fallback
formula.essential: soft halo on a slow bezier hover

task.is: a website button (a UI control that triggers an action) whose hover state animates along custom cubic-bezier curves
ladder: this button's values (curves, durations, halo, reduced-motion fallback)
job: write its CSS states (rest, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled)
make the motion practical (compositor-friendly, reduced-motion, touch)
check the result against the prompt

readings.reading: primary call-to-action button with hover, focus and active states

ak-neon-glow.instead: A low-saturation halo that brightens and fades with no hard edge.

ak-sense-button-hardware.excluded_sense: physical push button or hardware key
ak-sense-button-hardware.instead: website UI control: a call-to-action button with rest, hover, focus and active states

ak-sense-ethereal-transparency.instead: light and weightless: soft glow and depth

ak-default-ease.instead: A named custom cubic-bezier token with a slow settle, with its own duration for hover in and hover out.

ak-bounce-cta.instead: A soft settle with no overshoot, or at most one gentle return that stays inside the button's bounds.

ak-transition-all.instead: Transition only named properties, such as transform, opacity, and filter or a pseudo-element shadow.

ak-layout-animation.term: animating width, height, top or left
ak-layout-animation.instead: Animate transform (translate, scale) and opacity; fake size change with scale.

ak-shadow-blur-frames.instead: Fade opacity on a pre-drawn halo layer, so the blur is not recomputed every frame.

ak-no-reduced-motion.instead: A prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block that removes drift and keeps only a color or opacity change.

ak-hover-only.instead: Pair every :hover look with a matching :focus-visible state, and give touch an :active press state.

k-button-hover-bezier.text: Does the button's hover rule use a cubic-bezier timing function on its transition?

test.spec: a :hover rule whose transition or animation uses cubic-bezier(

k-dreamlike-light.text: Does the hover read as soft light or translucent float rather than a hard outline?

test.spec: the hover adds a halo or translucent light, not a solid border

k-practical-properties.text: Is only transform and opacity animated in the hover rule?

test.spec: transition lists containing width, height, top, left or all: count 0

k-no-transition-all.text: Does the transition name its properties instead of using all?

k-no-layout-animation.text: Is no layout property animated on hover?

k-glow-not-neon.text: Is the halo low-saturation with no hard edge rather than a neon outline?

test.spec: the box-shadow colour is muted and blurred, with no spread-only hard ring

k-reduced-motion-present.text: Is there a prefers-reduced-motion block that removes the movement?

test.spec: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block present, count at least 1

k-reduced-motion-keeps-colour.text: Under reduced motion, do colour and shadow changes survive while transform goes?

test.spec: the reduced-motion block drops transform and keeps colour or shadow change

k-focus-visible.text: Does keyboard focus get its own visible ring independent of hover?

k-target-size.text: Is the button at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels?

test.spec: min-height or min-width of 44px or larger on the button

k-hover-duration-band.text: Does the hover transition run within a short band that reads as response, not lag?

test.spec: hover transition duration between 200 ms and 800 ms

k-overshoot-gentle.text: Does any overshoot curve stay gentle, returning without a visible bounce?

test.spec: control points keep y close to 0 to 1 for the hover curve

k-one-hero-caveat.text: Is the sweep or glow limited to one hero call to action, with secondary buttons calm?

test.spec: only the primary button carries the glow or sweep

k-no-blur-frames.text: Is box-shadow not animated frame by frame on large surfaces?

test.spec: a box-shadow change on hover is kept short or moved to a pseudo-element opacity change

k-hover-only-guarded.text: Are hover-only effects guarded so touch users get an equivalent?

test.spec: @media (hover: hover) wraps hover-only effects, or a focus or active equivalent exists

k-label-contrast.text: Does the label keep readable contrast on the filled button?

test.spec: label contrast ratio at least 4.5:1 against the fill in rest and hover

k-sweep-streak-clipped.text: Is any sweep streak clipped to the button and ignoring the pointer?

k-no-glossy-hard-ring.text: Is there no hard ring that reads as a glowing outline?

request._about: Every requirement in the user's prompt, verbatim spans.

req-bezier-hover.anchor: custom bezier curve hover state animations
req-bezier-hover.text: The hover state animates along custom bezier curves.

req-dreamlike.anchor: makes it feel dreamlike and ethereal
req-dreamlike.text: The animation makes the button feel dreamlike and ethereal.

req-practical.text: The result must be practical for a website.

ux_principles._about: Discipline primer for the button: principles, motion accessibility, target and contrast rules, button states. Options, not requirements, where marked inferred.

ux-fitts-law.text: Time to reach a target grows with distance and shrinks with target size, so the button needs room and a generous hit area.
behaviors: Padding that enlarges the click area helps the button without changing its visual size
ux-fitts-law.principle: Size and proximity decide how fast a control is hit.
signals: small hit area on a primary action

ux-hick-law.text: Decision time rises with the number of choices, so one clearly primary button beats several equal ones.
behaviors: A hovered primary button draws the eye only if its siblings stay quiet
ux-hick-law.principle: Fewer competing options speed the choice.
signals: several equally styled buttons in one group

ux-motion-2-3-3.text: Non-essential motion that a user interaction triggers can be switched off; a hover glow that drifts is non-essential.
behaviors: A hover drift counts as non-essential, so it needs a reduced-motion path
ux-motion-2-3-3.principle: Motion caused by interaction can be turned off unless the motion carries information.
signals: hover movement with no reduced-motion fallback

ux-reduced-motion.text: The CSS media query lets the page honor an operating-system motion setting; the WCAG page lists it as a sufficient technique.
behaviors: Under reduced motion the hover keeps colour and shadow changes and drops the drift and bezier travel
ux-reduced-motion.principle: Honor the user's motion setting before adding any motion.

ux-target-contrast.text: Pointer targets reach 44 by 44 CSS pixels in the enhanced criterion, and UI component boundaries need 3:1 contrast with adjacent colours.
behaviors: A glow-only button edge that falls under 3:1 against the page fails the component contrast check
ux-target-contrast.principle: Size and edge contrast keep the control findable and hittable.
signals: button box under 44 px tall on touch

ux-perceived-response.text: Feedback within a fraction of a second feels immediate, so hover and press changes should start at once and stay short.
behaviors: A slow release on hover can read as lag if the press response is also slow
ux-perceived-response.principle: Motion should confirm input, not make the user wait for it.

ux-button-states.text: Rest, hover, focus-visible, active and disabled each need a distinct look, and focus should stay visible without the hover effect.
behaviors: Keyboard focus shows a ring even when the pointer never hovers
Disabled drops hover motion entirely
ux-button-states.principle: Every state answers a different question for the user.

motion-research._about: Curves, durations and cost for the button hover. Sources partly secondary; status shows which values are sourced.

rung-curves.text: Ease-out expo and back/overshoot curves are the common named families for hover feedback; values differ between sources, so verify before shipping.
behaviors: A steep ease-out curve front-loads motion so the hover reads as a quick, airy release
An overshoot curve (y above 1) lifts past the target then settles
rung-curves.principle: The curve sets the character of a motion more than its length does.
rung-curves.never_implies: Exact values are from secondary npm and gist sources, not easings.net.

rung-durations.text: Hover feedback sits in a short band; longer times read as lag, not dream.
properties: slow release 500-800ms for ambient glow only
behaviors: Durations past about 400ms on hover make the control feel slow to respond

rung-compositor.text: Transform and opacity are the only properties that animate without layout or paint; box-shadow and filter are paint-stage.
behaviors: Animating a glow via box-shadow repaints each frame, so animate opacity on a pseudo-element instead
rung-compositor.principle: Keep moving parts on the compositor so the glow does not cost frames.

rung-will-change.text: Promote only the element that animates; each layer costs memory, and blanket promotion can hurt on low-end devices.
behaviors: will-change on every button in a list multiplies layer memory
rung-will-change.principle: Promotion is a cost traded for smoothness; spend it on the one moving element.

rung-blur-cost.text: backdrop-filter and large blurs cost paint work per frame; sources here did not confirm this.
signals: frame drops when a blurred button sits over animating content
behaviors: Animating a blur radius repaints the layer every frame, which drops frames on low-end devices
A static backdrop blur with an animated opacity overlay keeps per-frame work to compositing
rung-blur-cost.never_implies: No fetched source measured backdrop-filter cost; treat as a profile-it item.

rung-glow-vocab.text: Words people use for this feel: ethereal, luminous, airy, floaty, dreamy, soft light, slow release.
signals: a soft halo, slow ease-out settle, faint translucency

motion_curves._about: Cubic-bezier curves and durations as Rails Designer publishes them in its hover examples (fetched 2026-11-05). Values are the page's own examples, not a standard.

where.heading_path: Level up CSS transitions with cubic-bezier > Examples that make a difference

rb-overshoot-curves.text: The page's hover examples use control points with negative or above-1 y values, which overshoot the target and settle back.
behaviors: A negative first y pulls the motion back before it starts, so the element dips first
A y above 1 carries the element past its end state, then it settles
rb-overshoot-curves.principle: Negative and above-1 control values create the bounce the page calls premium.
rb-overshoot-curves.never_implies: The page does not name these curves; the families and feel come from the author's examples.

rb-smooth-in-out.term: smooth in-out curve for a translate

where.heading_path: Level up CSS transitions with cubic-bezier > Examples that make a difference

rb-smooth-in-out.text: A symmetric curve with values between 0 and 1 moves a pill sideways with no overshoot.
behaviors: Both y values stay within 0 to 1, so the motion eases in and out without bounce
rb-smooth-in-out.principle: A curve that stays inside the box gives a calm settle; a curve that leaves the box gives character.

where.heading_path: Level up CSS transitions with cubic-bezier > Examples that make a difference

rb-durations.text: The examples run 0.3s for a bouncy scale and 0.5s for bouncy rotate and smooth translate; the closing advice uses 300ms.

where.heading_path: Level up CSS transitions with cubic-bezier

rb-ease-baseline.text: The page calls the default ease generic and flat; Tailwind offers ease-in, ease-out and ease-in-out classes as better defaults.
tools: Easing Wizard: drag control points and copy the cubic-bezier values

glow_button._about: Found on shadcnblocks.com: the Button Glow 1 example. Only what the page states; no transition timing or easing is given on the page.

sc-glow-treatment.text: A primary button with a colored glow shadow that intensifies on hover, the primary color at 40% opacity rising to 60%.
behaviors: The glow grows stronger on hover; the page does not describe it moving or lifting
sc-glow-treatment.principle: The glow marks a primary call to action and deepens on hover.
signals: colored halo behind a primary button

sc-glow-hover-timing-not-stated.text: The page gives no transition duration, easing curve or cubic-bezier for this button; the only stated change is the opacity rise.
signals: no timing values on the page
sc-glow-hover-timing-not-stated.principle: Durations and curves for this button must come from another source or be chosen by the builder.

sc-glow-use.text: Ideal as a hero CTA or in any dark-themed section where the glow provides visual hierarchy.
sc-glow-use.principle: The glow earns its place where it sets the main action apart.
signals: glow button used as hero call to action
glow button on a dark section

sc-glow-stack.text: Shipped as a shadcn/ui component built with React and Tailwind CSS, installed with the shadcn CLI, and listed for Radix UI, Base UI and React Aria.

shine_sweep._about: Hover behavior of one example button on a web page (Visual Library, shine sweep). Quoted or read from the fetched page source; a single example, not a standard.

sweep-motion.text: On hover a diagonal streak moves once across the button, animating only transform.
behaviors: The streak sits outside the left edge until hover, hidden by overflow hidden

streak-gradient.text: A soft white diagonal band, not a glow: a 120 degree gradient fading from transparent to 0.4 white and back. The page describes a streak, never a glow or blur.
properties: no blur or box-shadow in the CSS
signals: one bright band crossing the button

timing-variants.text: The page gives 800 ms as the premium default, with faster, slower and steeper alternatives.
behaviors: 400 ms reads as snappy or playful
1400 ms feels luxurious but can drag
skewX -30deg reads as sportier
skewX 0deg is rare and cleaner for minimalist sites

clipping-and-pointer.text: The button clips the streak with overflow hidden, and the streak ignores pointer events.

use-caveat.text: Use for one hero call to action per page; secondary buttons stay calm.
behaviors: Sweeping every button loses the effect's meaning

motion._about: Hover motion for the button: readings of the curve and dreamlike qualities, curve values with their sources, durations, and the properties that move. Options are builder choices, not requirements.

options._about: options, not requirements: builder choices where the prompt and evidence are silent

dec-lift-glow-drift.text: Lift moves the button up and grows its shadow; glow changes only light and leaves position still; drift offsets a halo slowly behind the button.
options: lift: translate -2 to -4 px and a soft shadow
glow: opacity on a halo, no movement
drift: halo offset 4 to 8 px on a long curve
dec-lift-glow-drift.tradeoffs: Lift reads most clearly as a response but moves the label; glow is safest for legibility and cheapest; drift adds the most dreamlike feel but needs the most care for focus and reduced motion.

dec-one-vs-staged.text: One curve moves every property together; staged curves give each property its own curve and delay.
options: one curve for transform and opacity together
staged: transform on a fast curve, glow on a slow curve with 80 to 150 ms delay
dec-one-vs-staged.tradeoffs: One curve is simpler and easier to check. Staged curves feel more layered, but the more properties animate, the more a page must budget for them.

dec-asymmetric-out.text: Use one curve for hover-in and a different, slower one for hover-out.
dec-asymmetric-out.tradeoffs: Asymmetry gives the release its own drift; a matching pair is easier to predict.

pool-slow-drift.text: Candidate curves for a long decelerating settle, to be tried and compared.

pool-soft-pulse.text: Candidate symmetric curves for a glow that rises and falls without a hard stop.

pool-delayed-bloom.text: Candidate curves for a glow that opens after a short delay.
options: delay 100 ms then cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) at 400 ms
delay 150 ms then cubic-bezier(0.19, 1, 0.22, 1) at 500 ms

pool-gentle-overshoot.text: Candidate curves with a small y above 1, so the overshoot stays brief.

motion-quality-readings.text: The word dreamlike can be read four ways for a hover; each gives a different curve shape and timing. Pick one or combine them.

readings.in_practice: A long ease-out (about 500 to 800 ms) that decelerates gently so the button seems to drift into its hover pose.
Opacity or glow rises and falls once with a smooth in-out curve, with no hard stop at the peak.
The glow waits about 80 to 150 ms after the pointer arrives, then opens over 300 to 500 ms.
A small control-point y above 1 (for example 1.2 to 1.4) lifts the button slightly past its target, then it settles back.

motion-curve-values.term: cubic-bezier values seen in hover examples
motion-curve-values.text: Curves with control points inside the 0 to 1 box settle without bounce; curves that leave the box overshoot or pull back first.
properties: cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.6, 0.32, 1.6) for a dip then overshoot
behaviors: A negative first y dips the element before it moves, which can read as anticipation
A y above 1 carries the element past its end state, then it returns
motion-curve-values.principle: Control points inside the box give a calm settle; points outside it give character, so use them sparingly on a website.
motion-curve-values.never_implies: These are the example values of one author's page, not a standard curve set.

motion-properties.text: Transform and opacity animate without layout or paint; box-shadow and filter repaint each frame. A glow can animate through opacity on a pseudo-element.
behaviors: Animating box-shadow each frame repaints the page, so keep a glow static and fade its opacity
Only the moving element needs will-change
motion-properties.principle: Keep moving parts on the compositor so the glow does not cost frames.
signals: opacity and transform only in the transition list

motion-rest-state.text: The rest state stays still when the pointer leaves, unless a reading asks for an idle breath.
behaviors: Hover-out returns the button to its rest transform and opacity on the same curve family
An idle breath runs forever and competes with the content, so it sits behind a reading and reduced-motion guard
signals: rest transform equals the value before hover

motion-durations.text: Hover-in speed is a reading choice: a quick response (200 to 320 ms) or a slow drift (500 to 800 ms). Hover-out can run slower than hover-in in either reading.

readings.in_practice: lift and glow answer the pointer within 200 to 320 ms
the glow settles over 500 to 800 ms while the lift stays quick
signals: reads as dreamy rather than responsive

behaviors: In the quick reading, hover-in past about 400 ms reads as lag rather than dream
In the slow drift reading, only the glow takes the long timing; the lift keeps the quick one
A slower hover-out lets the glow fade after the pointer leaves

surface._about: Surface, glow and haze for a dreamlike button. Values are illustrative starting points to check on the page, not sourced specs. Options, not requirements, where marked.

surf-readings.text: Ethereal can mean a glow that escapes the edge, a fill that lets blur show through, an edgeless light, or a haze that brightens.

readings.in_practice: A colored halo spreads outside the box with a large blur and low alpha, so the edge looks lit from behind.
signals: box-shadow or halo extends beyond the box

readings.in_practice: A semi-transparent fill sits over a backdrop blur, so the page behind softens and tints the button.
A radial highlight fades to transparent inside the button, so no hard outline shows.
signals: no solid border or a border near 10 percent alpha

readings.in_practice: A low-contrast veil lifts in opacity or lightness on hover, so the button seems to glow up from within.

surf-readings.principle: Ethereal is a set of readings of light and depth, and a build can combine two or three of them.

surf-fill.text: The fill can be a translucent tint over blur or a solid color with light added on top.
behaviors: A translucent fill lets the page behind shift color through the button, so it reads as a pane of light
A solid fill with a radial highlight keeps the label on a fixed color, so contrast holds on every page
surf-fill.principle: Translucency moves the background into the button; a solid base keeps the label readable.

surf-text-contrast.text: The label keeps its contrast against the fill; the glow stays outside the box and does not sit under the text.
behaviors: A glow that spills onto the label lowers contrast, so keep the halo outside the box edge
A translucent fill over a bright page can drop the label below 4.5 to 1, so check the lightest background
surf-text-contrast.principle: The effect serves the label; the label keeps its own contrast.
signals: label below 4.5 to 1 on the lightest background

surf-light-source.text: Light on the button is a soft highlight inside the box or a thin luminous outline; the readings differ on whether the edge carries the light.

readings.in_practice: a radial highlight fades to transparent before the edge; no outline
a solid or thin luminous border traces the shape and carries the light
signals: light reads on the edge rather than inside

behaviors: In the edgeless reading, a highlight that fades to transparent before the edge removes the visible outline
In the edgeless reading, a border near 10 percent white keeps the shape legible on dark pages without a hard line
surf-light-source.principle: In the edgeless reading, light without an edge reads as luminous; an edge makes it read as a shape.

surf-glow-halo.text: A halo in the primary hue, raised in opacity and spread on hover. The readings differ on whether it bleeds past the edge or stays inside the box.

readings.in_practice: a blurred halo sits outside the box and fades with distance
the glow fills the box from inside with soft falloff; no light leaves the edge
signals: glow contained within the box edges

behaviors: A halo placed in a pseudo-element with opacity 0 to 1 on hover animates without repainting the button
Raising spread and alpha together reads as a brighter glow; raising alpha alone reads as a stronger shadow
surf-glow-halo.principle: In the halo-bleeding reading, glow is light leaving the object, so it sits outside the edge and fades with distance.

states_and_access._about: Button states, reduced-motion and touch fallbacks, contrast and target size, and what makes motion too fast, too slow or too busy. Inferred where no source is cited.

st-rest-hover.text: Rest is still; hover changes colour, glow and shadow, and any drift or lift is a separate, reducible layer.
behaviors: Hover adds light or shadow first; movement is optional and reduced-motion removes it
st-rest-hover.principle: Rest must stay readable on its own; hover only adds emphasis.
st-rest-hover.never_implies: hover alone shows the button is clickable

st-focus-visible.text: Keyboard focus gets its own visible ring that does not depend on hover, so focus shows the same effect as hover.
behaviors: A keyboard user who never hovers still sees the focus ring
st-focus-visible.principle: Focus is a separate state from hover and needs its own mark.
st-focus-visible.never_implies: a hover glow is enough focus indication

st-active-disabled.text: Active presses the button down briefly and returns it; disabled drops hover motion and glow entirely.
behaviors: A disabled button ignores hover and shows no drift
st-active-disabled.principle: Press confirms input fast; disabled must not invite interaction.

rm-reduced-motion.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion the hover keeps colour and shadow changes and drops transform travel, drift and bezier movement.
behaviors: Reduced motion swaps the bezier transition for an instant or fade change
rm-reduced-motion.principle: Interaction-triggered motion can be turned off unless it carries information.
signals: no reduced-motion block near button rules

touch-hover-media.text: Hover is not reliable on touch; wrap hover-only effects in a hover media query and give touch a tap or focus equivalent.
behaviors: On touch the glow appears on press, not on hover, and nothing depends on hover to show the label
touch-hover-media.principle: Touch has no hover; an effect that carries meaning must work without it.

pace-signals.term: too fast, too slow, too busy
pace-signals.text: Too fast reads as a flicker; too slow reads as lag; too busy means drift or glow runs while the user is not interacting.
behaviors: A hover that takes over 600 ms makes the press feel late
pace-signals.principle: Motion should confirm input without making the user wait or watch.

req-practical-quality.text: Practical has four readings; a website button should satisfy all of them, and each has signals to check.

readings.in_practice: animate only transform and opacity so the compositor does the work
visible focus, 3:1 edge, 44px target, reduced-motion path
no meaning carried by hover alone
label contrast holds when the glow is at full strength

ct-contrast-target.text: Keep the button at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels and its edge at 3:1 against the page, so the glow does not replace a visible boundary.
behaviors: A glow-only edge under 3:1 fails the component contrast check
ct-contrast-target.principle: The control has to be findable and hittable before it is pretty.

lexicon._about: Brain-dump associations for the button's feel, motion and site fit. Seed material, tier 3-4 unless a fetched source backs it.

lx-quality-bezier-hover.text: The easing is a hand-set cubic-bezier, so the shape of the motion (fast in, slow out, overshoot) is chosen, not the browser default.

readings.in_practice: cubic-bezier with a low first control point, e.g. (0.3, 0, 0.2, 1), for a gradual start
cubic-bezier (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), most motion in the first 40%
cubic-bezier (0.34, 1.3, 0.64, 1) with y above 1, a small pass then return
different curves for transform, opacity and shadow, so glow lags lift

contribution: Apple spring-based UI motion: interruptible settle, momentum that eases out
Material motion guidance: standard easing curves, responsive timing, continuity between states

placement._about: Where the button sits on a page. Options, not requirements: covers the job step 'place it on a page'.

pl-page-placement.text: Where the button sits decides how much glow and motion it can carry: a hero call-to-action, an inline text button, or a sticky bar button.
behaviors: A hero call-to-action can carry the full halo; one per screen keeps it the focus
An inline text button should keep its halo small so the surrounding line does not shift
A sticky bar button stays in view while scrolling, so its glow must stay quiet at rest or it competes with the content
signals: large type and one button per screen (hero)
fixed to the viewport edge (sticky bar)

s-webdev-compositor.title: Stick to compositor-only properties and manage layer count (web.dev)
s-webdev-compositor.quote: Today there are only two properties for which that is true - transforms and opacity

s-webdev-layers.title: Stick to compositor-only properties and manage layer count (web.dev)
s-webdev-layers.quote: every layer you create requires memory and management, and that's not free

s-railsdesigner.title: Level up CSS transitions with cubic-bezier | Rails Designer
s-railsdesigner.quote: Notice the negative values in the cubic-bezier functions? Those create the “bounce” effect that overshoots its target before settling into place

s-shadcnblocks-glow-1.title: Button Glow 1 - Glow primary - Shadcnblocks.com
s-shadcnblocks-glow-1.quote: The glow uses the primary color at 40% opacity, expanding to 60% on hover.

s-visual-library-shine.title: Shine sweep on button hover - Visual Library
s-visual-library-shine.quote: Faster (0.4s) reads as snappy/playful. Slower (1.4s) feels luxurious but can drag.
